policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: "unto Cos" renders either accusative spelling of the island's name; ASV shows no difference.
"when we had come in sight of Cyprus" fits either aorist participle form of ἀναφαίνω equally.
"we sailed unto Syria, and landed at Tyre" renders the active "came down" or the passive "were brought down" alike; ASV does not mark the voice.
Greek word order of subject and verb in "there the ship was to unlade her burden" leaves no trace in the English.
ASV "And having found the disciples" renders δέ and καί alike, and English "the" is not a reliable index of the Greek article.
ASV "that he should not set foot in Jerusalem" renders ἐπιβαίνειν; ἀναβαίνειν would give "go up to Jerusalem".
ASV spells "Jerusalem" uniformly; the Ἱεροσόλυμα/Ἱερουσαλήμ difference is invisible in English.
"when it came to pass that we had accomplished the days" is the same English under either order of infinitive and pronoun.
ASV "we prayed, and bade each other farewell" coordinates finite verbs, which renders a participle chain as readily as a finite προσηυξάμεθα.

ASV ends v.5 with the finite "bade each other farewell" and opens v.6 with "and we went on board", excluding RP's participial καὶ ἀσπασάμενοι ἀλλήλους attached to the boarding; base and r01 differ only in punctuation, which ASV cannot show.
"we went on board the ship" renders ἐνέβημεν, ἀνέβημεν or ἐπέβημεν indifferently.
ASV keeps the first person, "we departed, and came unto Caesarea"; RP's οἱ περὶ τὸν Παῦλον ἦλθον would give "they that were of Paul's company came".
"four virgin daughters" fixes English order regardless of the Greek order of numeral and noun.
"as we tarried there some days" supplies the subject of the genitive absolute in English whether or not ἡμῶν stands in the Greek.
"he bound his own feet and hands" renders reflexive ἑαυτοῦ and τε αὐτοῦ alike; "own" is idiomatic English for the possessor already named.
"Then Paul answered" serves as a rendering of τότε and of the connective τε; the English adverb does not settle which stood in the Greek.
"The will of the Lord be done" is the required English order under either Greek arrangement.
"be done" does not mark present γινέσθω against aorist γενέσθω.
"went up to Jerusalem" is the same for either spelling; the verse's only note is an alternative rendering of the baggage clause and does not touch this unit.
"the brethren received us gladly" renders the compound ἀπεδέξαντο and the simplex ἐδέξαντο alike.
ASV "glorified God" renders θεόν; κύριον would give "the Lord".
"and they said unto him" renders a coordinated finite εἶπόν τε or the participle εἰπόντες; ASV regularly resolves such participles into finite clauses.
ASV "how many thousands there are among the Jews of them that have believed" renders the prepositional ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις; the genitive Ἰουδαίων would give "thousands of Jews that believe".
ASV "What is it therefore? they will certainly hear that thou art come" has no counterpart to RP's δεῖ πλῆθος συνελθεῖν, "the multitude must needs come together".
ASV "four men that have a vow on them" renders ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτῶν; ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτῶν would mean the vow was taken of their own accord.
"that they may shave their heads" renders the future indicative and the aorist subjunctive after ἵνα alike.
ASV breaks the purpose clause with an assertion, "and all shall know", which renders the future indicative γνώσονται; the subjunctive γνῶσιν would continue the ἵνα as "and all may know".
"keeping the law" fixes English order whichever way participle and object stand in the Greek.
ASV "we wrote", with margin "Or, enjoined", renders ἐπεστείλαμεν; the note reports "sent" (ἀπεστείλαμεν) as a reading of other authorities, not the text.
ASV "giving judgment that they should keep themselves from things sacrificed to idols" has nothing for RP's μηδὲν τοιοῦτον τηρεῖν αὐτούς εἰ μή, "that they observe no such thing, save only".
"and from what is strangled" shows nothing of an article before πνικτόν.
"laid hands on him" is the same English under either order of the prepositional phrase and object.
"everywhere" renders πανταχῇ and πανταχοῦ alike.
ASV "they had before seen with him in the city Trophimus" renders the compound προεωρακότες; the simplex ἑωρακότες would give only "had seen".
ASV opens "And as they were seeking to kill him", which renders τε or δέ indifferently.
"that all Jerusalem was in confusion" in indirect discourse does not distinguish the present συγχύννεται from the perfect συγκέχυται.
"Then the chief captain came near" serves for τότε and for the connective δέ alike.
"inquired who he was" gives no separate rendering of ἄν.
"some shouted one thing, some another" renders ἐπεφώνουν and ἐβόων alike.
"when he could not know the certainty" renders the genitive absolute and the nominative participle alike; ASV supplies "he" either way.
"the multitude of the people followed after, crying out" shows nothing of whether the participle agrees ad sensum in the plural or with πλῆθος in the neuter singular.
ASV "May I say something unto thee?" renders τι; the RP omission would give simply "May I speak unto thee?".
"he spake unto them in the Hebrew language" does not distinguish the aorist προσεφώνησεν from the imperfect προσεφώνει.
